root_motivation: Joe's mcphost gate takes 21–42 minutes for a 413 s cold compile. The repo's `tests/` directory holds 289 top-level `.rs` files (2026-09-12 count) and cargo's default `autotests` makes each one a separate test binary; each links the whole 52K-LoC crate and its 41 dependencies, and measured binaries are 274–291 MB (`attrib_ac1_loopback_signup_unstamped`, `infer_ac08_ac09_python_requirements`). `target/debug/deps` holds 1,391 such binaries. 269 of the files declare `mod common;`, so the shared helper is compiled 269 times. RedBaron's root disk reached 81–86 % on 09-08, with `target/` dirs the known bulk. Every gate pays the link cost 289 times for one crate; every new AC PRD adds another binary. PRD-build-gate-phase-timing measures the `gate` phase this PRD moves; until it ships, the expected saving is inferred from binary count and size, not measured.
user_persona: The loop dispatching mcphost's gate: it pays the whole-crate link cost ~289 times per gate today (21-42 minutes for a 413 s cold compile), and every new AC PRD that adds one tests/<prefix>_ac<N>_*.rs file adds another binary. Also the AC-pairing classifier, which resolves tests/<prefix>_ac<N>_*.rs paths and must see the same file names and paths after consolidation as before, and the operator watching RedBaron's root disk (81-86% on 2026-09-08, target/ the known bulk).

scope: `Cargo.toml`: `autotests = false`; one `[[test]]` per area with `path = "tests/suite_<area>.rs"`; areas chosen by filename prefix so no suite exceeds ~60 files and the total is <=10 (AC1).

`scripts/gen-test-suites.sh`: scans top-level `tests/*.rs`, assigns each to an area by prefix table, writes `tests/suite_<area>.rs` with `#[path = "<file>.rs"] mod <ident>;` lines plus one shared `mod common;` (and `support`, `ci_sandbox_support` where used); deterministic, sorted output; `--check` exits non-zero naming any unregistered or drifted file, wired into ci-checks (AC1/AC2).
Per-file `mod common;` (and the other helper declarations) removed from included files, replaced by `use crate::common;` or equivalent so the helper compiles once (AC3).

Every test that ran before runs after: nextest's test list, suite prefix stripped, equals the pre-change list; the verified-completed pairing classifier and intent-card test pointers resolve exactly as before (AC1/AC4).
non_goals: Changing any test's body or assertion, or `src/`.
Changing the runner: nextest stays, and its per-test process isolation is what keeps host-independence fixes valid.
Reducing the number of test files. Consolidation is at the binary level only.

additional.no_src_change: Engineering target explicitly excludes src/ changes; only Cargo.toml, tests/suite_*.rs, the helper declarations, and scripts/ are touched.
additional.test_identity_preserved: nextest's test list, with the suite prefix stripped, must equal the set listed at the parent commit -- consolidation renames no test and drops none (AC1/AC4 guardrail).

five_whys_trace.q: Why does mcphost's gate take 21-42 minutes for a 413 s cold compile?
five_whys_trace.a: cargo links roughly 289 separate test binaries every run (one per top-level tests/*.rs file), each 274-291 MB.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does cargo build ~289 separate binaries for one crate's tests?
five_whys_trace.a: Cargo's default `autotests = true` makes every top-level tests/*.rs file its own compilation unit and its own binary; nothing in the repo opts out of that default.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is each of those binaries so expensive to link?
five_whys_trace.a: Each one separately links the whole 52K-LoC crate and its 41 dependencies, and 269 of the 289 files declare `mod common;`, so the shared test helper is compiled 269 times over instead of once.

five_whys_trace.q: Why has this not already been fixed?
five_whys_trace.a: No PRD had previously consolidated the binaries; each new AC PRD just added one more tests/<prefix>_ac<N>_*.rs file under the existing autotests default, silently growing both the gate's link cost and target/debug/deps's disk footprint.

five_whys_trace.q: Why fix it now rather than wait for PRD-build-gate-phase-timing to measure the exact saving first?
five_whys_trace.a: RedBaron's root disk already reached 81-86% on 2026-09-08 with target/ as the known bulk, and every gate on this repo keeps paying the per-binary link cost in the meantime; the expected saving is inferred from binary count and size today, and PRD-build-gate-phase-timing verifies it once both ship -- it does not need to land first to justify shipping this PRD.
